newsitem.title: UK: Brent Walker calls for betting deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Brent Walker calls for betting deregulation.

text.p: The Brent Walker Group Plc said worries over the state of the UK's betting industry would continue unless there was further deregulation and cuts in taxes on betting.
"The continuing decrease in turnover (at its William Hill betting shop chain) is of great concern to us," chairman Sir Brian Goswell said in a statement.
"Unless further deregulation and decreases in betting duty are implemented by the government to redress the competitive advantages of the National Lottery, this concern can only increase," he added.
The National Lottery was introduced nearly two years ago and has outperformed expectations on profits, hitting the betting industry.
Brent Walker steadied its first half pretax loss at 51.6 million pounds and passed on its dividend.
The betting shops to pubs chain saw turnover slip to 852.6 million pounds from 861.9 million previously.
The group said it initiatives such as "Lucky Choice," which is betting on Ireland's lottery, would continue in an effort to boost profitability.
It said it was still too early to gauge the impact on profits of "Amusement with Prizes" machines which were introduced into betting shops at the end of June, but "early signs were encouraging."

It said public house turnover was up 10.7 percent despite a fall in the number of houses in the tenanted estate, while operating profit before exceptional items rose 11.2 percent to 8.9 million pounds.
